currentContext.business: The Company manufactures bearings and bearing components in India, having added new capacity across spherical roller bearings and cylindrical roller bearings and taking its localization efforts to new heights, which helped it take on more business through reduced lead times and additional credentials to qualify under Make in India initiatives. It is investing at its Bharuch facility to produce plain bearings using Fiber reinforced composite (FRC) material to strengthen its position in the plain bearing market, and its Jamshedpur manufacturing facilities serve the rail market. The Company is well connected to the core sectors and capital goods market and is deeply entrenched through its direct and indirect sales and service models, and during the year advanced further in the Process OEMs and Distribution segment.

currentContext.expansion: The Company invested in new capacity addition across spherical roller bearings and cylindrical roller bearings, taking its localization efforts to new heights; the new capacities helped take on more business on the back of reduced lead times and with additional credentials to qualify under Make in India initiatives. The defining milestone of the year was the inauguration of the Bharuch manufacturing facility, which the Chairman describes as reflecting confidence in India's long-term industrial growth and a commitment to building world-class manufacturing capabilities closer to customers, enhancing the ability to serve customers with a broader product portfolio, improved responsiveness and greater manufacturing flexibility. Bringing the new site online requires patience and perseverance, and as the Bharuch facility ramps up the Company continues to incur initial operating costs and fund capability building, which it views through a long-term lens. The Bharuch new plant was capitalized during the year, and the Company continues with its expansion through investment in the Jamshedpur Rail project. During FY 2025-26 the Company allocated approximately 8% of its revenue for capital expenditures while maintaining a debt-free balance sheet and a healthy liquidity position, and it also acquired shares of Timken GGB Technology Private Limited and invested in the equity of a power producer company for procurement of electricity from renewable sources.

risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict and slowing global growth
risks.note: Global activity faces a major test from the outbreak of war in the Middle East, with global growth forecast to decelerate to 3.1 percent in 2026 from 3.4 percent in 2025 and a larger net impact expected on emerging markets; the Chairman also describes an environment marked by geopolitical uncertainties, evolving trade dynamics and changing industrial supply chains

India meets more than 85 percent of its crude oil requirements through imports with approximately half transiting the Strait of Hormuz, so the conflict poses the risk of a significant terms-of-trade shock that could increase input costs, exert downward pressure on the rupee, and complicate inflation-growth trade-offs

Profit before tax as a percentage of revenue from operations declined compared with the previous year mainly due to increased cost of material consumed, increased depreciation charges and reduction in other income, with net material cost rising modestly faster than revenue growth

risks.risk: Execution and ramp-up drag from the new Bharuch plant
risks.note: Bringing a new site online requires patience and perseverance; as Bharuch ramps up the Company continues to incur initial operating costs and fund capability building, and higher depreciation from the new manufacturing plant added to other expenses

risks.risk: Cyclicality and policy dependence of end markets
risks.note: Demand is tied to government capex and industry cycles — Indian Railways budgetary support, steel and cement capacity expansion, thermal PowerGen commissioning, mining output targets and infrastructure-led commercial vehicle demand — so any slowdown in public capex directly affects the bearing demand base

risks.risk: Pull-forward of tractor demand ahead of TREM V norms
risks.note: The record FY 2026 tractor upcycle was partly driven by pre-buying ahead of TREM V norms effective April 2026, which can borrow volumes from the following year even as the CV cycle is expected to moderate to efficiency-driven growth in FY 27

The Company runs material arm's length transactions with group entities — The Timken Company (Ultimate Holding Company, including royalty), The Timken Corporation and Timken Wuxi Bearings Co. Ltd. (fellow subsidiaries) — for purchases and sales of goods, making sourcing, offtake and technology access dependent on the parent group and requiring recurring Board and shareholder approvals

Revenue growth for the year was primarily driven by strong export sales with volume growth across geographical locations while domestic revenue showed modest growth, leaving the Company exposed to higher trade barriers and reconfiguration of trade flows and supply chains

one-line thesis: Timken India crossed INR 1,000 crore quarterly revenue for the first time in Q4FY26, driven by robust exports and CV demand, though margins faced pressure from rising input costs with only 10% price pass-through achieved so far. The strategic merger with Timken GGB and progressive ramp-up of the Bharuch plant (targeting 70% utilization by July) position the company for long-term synergy, despite near-term margin volatility as cost hikes are negotiated.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,073 cr (+14.2% YoY); EBITDA Margin: 18.7% (FY26 full year); PAT: Not explicitly broken out, PBT INR 207 cr (Q4) vs INR 21% margin prior year adjusted; Order Book: Healthy, specifically in Rail and Exports; Net Debt: Debt-free. One-offs: Labor code-related impact in current year; Previous year had BAPA adjustment excluded.
guidance: Revenue Growth: > Market growth (no specific %); Margin: Under pressure short-term due to inflation, expecting recovery via price hikes over next 2 quarters; Order Inflow: Strong in North America exports and Process industry; Capex: ~8-10% of revenue annually (INR 120 cr for Jamshedpur rail expansion).
order book & pipeline: Described as 'healthy' with specific strength in North American exports (Q4 exports INR 222 cr, +40% QoQ) and domestic Rail (Q4 INR 278 cr).
segment / subsidiary detail: Q4 Breakup: Rail 26% (INR 278 cr); Mobile (CV+Tractor) 19% (INR 205 cr); Process Industry 19% (INR 200 cr); Distribution 15% (INR 162 cr); Intercompany/Exports 21% (INR 222.5 cr). FY26 Total Revenue INR 3,419 cr.
growth verticals / optionality: Bharuch plant ramp-up (targeting 70% utilization by July FY27); Jamshedpur rail expansion going live by Dec FY26; Potential M&A; Expansion into larger bearing sizes and wind energy (5MW+).
margins & cost dynamics: Input costs (steel, grinding wheels, coolants) rising; Currency depreciation impacting imports; Price hike implementation started mid-April, only 10% realized so far, remaining 90% expected over next 2 quarters; Bharuch ramp-up costs near breakeven, impact reduced from Q3.
capex / expansion: FY26 Capex INR 297 cr (8.7% of revenue); FY27 guidance ~8-10% of revenue; INR 120 cr allocated for Jamshedpur rail expansion; Bharuch plant total investment ~INR 720 cr (INR 350 cr building, rest machinery).
capital allocation: Debt-free balance sheet; Merger of Timken GGB approved for synergies; Dividend reduced to INR 2.5/share (vs INR 36 previous special dividend) to prioritize reinvestment in growth projects.
risks & watch-items: Raw material inflation outpacing price pass-through; Delay in PPAP approvals for new plants; Geopolitical trade tensions affecting exports; Cyclical downturn in CV/Tractor segments; Rail project execution delays.
management quality / tone: Confident on demand stability and long-term strategy; Cautious on near-term margins due to cost inflation; Aggressive on capacity utilization and price realization efforts.
non-obvious takeaways: Export growth to North America is accelerating (+66% YoY) despite pending trade deals; Process industry (Steel/Cement) expected to outpace Mobile/Rail in growth rate over next 2 years due to India's industrialization shift; Bharuch plant building cost was ~50% of total capex, allowing future expansion within existing structure.

| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising steel and input costs squeezing margins until price hikes are fully realized | Competitors with weaker pricing power | loser | Med | Timken's ability to pass on 90% of pending price hikes over 2 quarters may force smaller players to absorb costs, losing market share. |
| Need for high-precision, ultra-high-speed rail bearings for future projects | Domestic Rail OEMs | beneficiary | High | Jamshedpur expansion (live Dec FY26) specifically targets state-of-the-art robotics for super-precision rail bearings, reducing import dependence. |
| Energy security and cost optimization in manufacturing | Timken India (Self) | beneficiary | High | Completed renewable energy investments across plants provide long-term cost insulation against power tariff hikes. |

hero.oneLiner: Timken India Limited is the Indian arm of The Timken Company, manufacturing and selling anti-friction bearings and related components for railways, core industrial sectors, commercial vehicles and tractors, serving both OEMs and the aftermarket through direct and indirect sales and service models.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Timken India Limited is the Indian arm of The Timken Company, manufacturing and selling anti-friction bearings and related components for railways, core industrial sectors, commercial vehicles and tractors, serving both OEMs and the aftermarket through direct and indirect sales and service models.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures bearings and bearing components in India, having added new capacity across spherical roller bearings and cylindrical roller bearings and taking its localization efforts to new heights, which helped it take on more business through reduced lead times and additional credentials to qualify under Make in India initiatives. It is investing at its Bharuch facility to produce plain bearings using Fiber reinforced composite (FRC) material to strengthen its position in the plain bearing market, and its Jamshedpur manufacturing facilities serve the rail market. The Company is well connected to the core sectors and capital goods market and is deeply entrenched through its direct and indirect sales and service models, and during the year advanced further in the Process OEMs and Distribution segment.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Timken GGB Technology Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary (100% shareholding), CIN U29130KA2007PTC203242, acquired on 1 December 2025 by paying cash consideration to sellers; the Board has approved a draft Scheme of Amalgamation to merge it with the Company. The Company's plain bearings line at Bharuch will be sold under the GGB brand name.
- Sunstreamgreen Energy C&I Three Private Limited — related party: Approximately 26% shareholding acquired to purchase power under the group captive scheme; the Company does not exercise significant influence and hence it is not an Associate under Section 2(6) of the Companies Act
- The Timken Company — related party: Ultimate Holding Company; arm's length transactions covering purchase and sale of goods, expenses, agency commission, purchase of property and equipment, and royalty. A resolution for estimated material related party transactions with The Timken Company is placed before the 39th AGM.
- The Timken Corporation — related party: Fellow Subsidiary; arm's length transactions covering purchase and sale of goods, purchase of property, plant and equipment, expenses and agency commission, based on transfer pricing guidelines / market rates for one year i.e. FY 2025-26
- Timken Wuxi Bearings Co. Ltd. — related party: Fellow Subsidiary; arm's length transactions covering purchase of goods, sale of goods and expenses
- Timken Engineering and Research India Private Limited (TERI) — related party: Transactions were estimated as material and shareholder approval was taken, but considering actual transaction amounts they do not qualify as material transactions
- ABC Bearings Limited — related party: Erstwhile company amalgamated with Timken India Limited; unclaimed interim dividend and fractional-share sale proceeds arising from the merger were transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's bearing market has been growing at a CAGR of over 9.4 percent and was valued at around USD 2.9 billion in FY 2026, driven by rising demand across automotive (CVs, tractors), railways, industrial machinery and renewable energy, and boosted by localization policies, electric-vehicle trends and infrastructure development
- In FY 2027 India's bearing market is expected to see steady, structurally driven growth, supported by continued core industry, railway and infrastructure capex, stable demand from commercial vehicles and tractors, and a resilient aftermarket that cushions volume volatility
- Rail market has shown strong demand and stability, supporting effective utilisation of the Jamshedpur facilities
- Indian Railways capital allocation of about 2.62 lakh crore in FY 2026 including 2.52 lakh crore budgetary support, with record coach output exceeding 9,900 coaches and 1,914 locomotive units in FY 26, reflecting continued priority on rail infrastructure and modernization
- Steel: crude steel output up 10.7% YoY to approximately 168.4 million tonnes in FY 26; steelmaking capacity of approximately 220 million tonnes in FY 2025-26 projected to reach 300 million tonnes by 2030, with public sector capex rising nearly 44%
- PowerGen: neutral sector outlook for FY 27 with long-term electricity demand growth of 5.5-6.0 percent YoY, thermal plant utilisation projected around 65 percent over FY 26-FY 27, around 5 GW of thermal capacity expected to be commissioned in FY 27 and about 39,545 MW under construction
- Wind: India added 6.34 GW of new onshore wind capacity in 2025, the highest annual addition since 2017 and an 85% increase over the previous year; global new wind installations estimated at 178 GW in 2026 with a 5.2% CAGR forecast for 2026-2030
- Cement: grinding capacity additions of 160-170 million tonnes estimated during fiscals 2026 to 2028 with incremental demand of approximately 30-40 million tonnes per annum
- Mining: raw coal production of 1.04 billion tonnes in FY 2026 with a target of 1.31 billion tonnes for FY 2026-27; iron ore production up 7% to a record 310 million tonnes
- Commercial vehicles: FY 2025-26 volumes crossed 1 million units on capex-led, infrastructure-anchored demand, creating a stable base for moderated, efficiency-driven growth in FY 27
- Tractors: FY 2026 was a breakout year with retail sales exceeding 10.5 lakh units, driven by rural tailwinds and pre-buying ahead of TREM V norms effective April 2026
- Capital goods sector supported by sustained government infrastructure spending and emphasis on manufacturing growth, reducing import dependence and strengthening supply chain resilience
- Structural drivers of India's infrastructure, manufacturing, railways and energy transition investments, combined with increasing localisation and supply-chain diversification, create significant opportunities for industrial companies with strong technology, manufacturing capabilities and customer relationships
- Highest-ever revenue in FY 2025-26 was driven primarily by strong export sales with volume growth across geographical locations, while domestic revenue showed modest growth
- Margin headwind from initial operating costs and capability-building funding as the Bharuch facility ramps up
- Macro risk from rising oil prices and geopolitical tension, given India imports more than 85 percent of its crude oil requirements with approximately half transiting the Strait of Hormuz, posing a terms-of-trade shock risk that could increase input costs and pressure the rupee

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Input costs (steel, grinding wheels, coolants) rising; Currency depreciation impacting imports; Price hike implementation started mid-April, only 10% realized so far, remaining 90% expected over next 2 quarters; Bharuch ramp-up costs near breakeven, impact reduced from Q3.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt-free balance sheet; Merger of Timken GGB approved for synergies; Dividend reduced to INR 2.5/share (vs INR 36 previous special dividend) to prioritize reinvestment in growth projects.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company invested in new capacity addition across spherical roller bearings and cylindrical roller bearings, taking its localization efforts to new heights; the new capacities helped take on more business on the back of reduced lead times and with additional credentials to qualify under Make in India initiatives. The defining milestone of the year was the inauguration of the Bharuch manufacturing facility, which the Chairman describes as reflecting confidence in India's long-term industrial growth and a commitment to building world-class manufacturing capabilities closer to customers, enhancing the ability to serve customers with a broader product portfolio, improved responsiveness and greater manufacturing flexibility. Bringing the new site online requires patience and perseverance, and as the Bharuch facility ramps up the Company continues to incur initial operating costs and fund capability building, which it views through a long-term lens. The Bharuch new plant was capitalized during the year, and the Company continues with its expansion through investment in the Jamshedpur Rail project. During FY 2025-26 the Company allocated approximately 8% of its revenue for capital expenditures while maintaining a debt-free balance sheet and a healthy liquidity position, and it also acquired shares of Timken GGB Technology Private Limited and invested in the equity of a power producer company for procurement of electricity from renewable sources.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on demand stability and long-term strategy; Cautious on near-term margins due to cost inflation; Aggressive on capacity utilization and price realization efforts.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Investments in new capacity across spherical roller bearings and cylindrical roller bearings have taken localization efforts to new heights, helping win more business on the back of reduced lead times and additional credentials to qualify under Make in India initiatives
- Effective utilisation of the Jamshedpur manufacturing facilities on the back of strong and stable rail demand, leading to improved production efficiency and cost management
- Deeply entrenched in core sectors and the capital goods market through direct and indirect sales and service models
- Part of the global Timken group, with The Timken Company as ultimate holding company and access to group technology under a royalty arrangement
- Debt-free balance sheet and healthy cash reserves while continuing to make strategic investments to support future growth
- Multiple awards and recognitions during the year including CII circle competitions, Best in class Manufacturing supply chain 2025, Yellow dot award 2025, Best Organizations to work 2025, Brand of the year award 2025, and recognition at the 2025 International Metallographic contest

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Raw material inflation outpacing price pass-through; Delay in PPAP approvals for new plants; Geopolitical trade tensions affecting exports; Cyclical downturn in CV/Tractor segments; Rail project execution delays.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Export growth to North America is accelerating (+66% YoY) despite pending trade deals; Process industry (Steel/Cement) expected to outpace Mobile/Rail in growth rate over next 2 years due to India's industrialization shift; Bharuch plant building cost was ~50% of total capex, allowing future expansion within existing structure.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expand the manufacturing footprint in India and build world-class manufacturing capabilities closer to customers, of which the inauguration of the Bharuch facility was described as a defining milestone
- Broaden the product portfolio and improve responsiveness and manufacturing flexibility through the Bharuch facility, viewed through a long-term lens while initial operating and capability-building costs are incurred during ramp-up

challenges.body:

| Rising steel and input costs squeezing margins until price hikes are fully realized | Competitors with weaker pricing power | loser | Med | Timken's ability to pass on 90% of pending price hikes over 2 quarters may force smaller players to absorb costs, losing market share. |
| Need for high-precision, ultra-high-speed rail bearings for future projects | Domestic Rail OEMs | beneficiary | High | Jamshedpur expansion (live Dec FY26) specifically targets state-of-the-art robotics for super-precision rail bearings, reducing import dependence. |
